name: convert_from_spdif_status
prose: Pure helper converting IEC958 status bits sbits (with the second status byte in bits 8 and up) into the HDA digital-converter control word. Returns an unsigned short built from: AC_DIG1_PROFESSIONAL if IEC958_AES0_PROFESSIONAL is set, AC_DIG1_NONAUDIO if IEC958_AES0_NONAUDIO is set. If the professional bit is set, AC_DIG1_EMPHASIS is set when (sbits & IEC958_AES0_PRO_EMPHASIS) equals IEC958_AES0_PRO_EMPHASIS_5015. Otherwise (consumer format) AC_DIG1_EMPHASIS is set when (sbits & IEC958_AES0_CON_EMPHASIS) equals IEC958_AES0_CON_EMPHASIS_5015, AC_DIG1_COPYRIGHT is set when IEC958_AES0_CON_NOT_COPYRIGHT is clear, AC_DIG1_LEVEL is set when IEC958_AES1_CON_ORIGINAL << 8 is set in sbits, and the category bits sbits & (IEC958_AES1_CON_CATEGORY << 8) are ORed in. It has no other return and no side effects.
note: codec.c:2190-2213. Reviewer only reported a Frama-C rejection of the old contract (right); contract left empty.

name: snd_cs4236_create
prose: Precondition: card, port, cport (control port), irq, dma1, dma2, hardware type, hwshare and rchip (output pointer). Sets *rchip = NULL first. A hardware value of WSS_HW_DETECT is changed to WSS_HW_DETECT3, then snd_wss_create is called and its negative error is returned if it fails. If the created chip's hardware does not match WSS_HW_CS4236B_MASK it stores the chip in *rchip and returns 0 without further setup. For a CS4236+ chip it returns -ENODEV if cport is below 0x100 or is SNDRV_AUTO_PORT (error message logged). It reads the version from control register C1 (snd_cs4236_ctrl_in) and from the extended register CS4236_VERSION and returns -ENODEV if they differ. Otherwise it writes control registers C0, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7 and C8 with fixed values (C5 and C6 built from IEC958 constants; C1 is only read, not written), installs rate_constraint, set_playback_format and set_capture_format callbacks (and suspend/resume under CONFIG_PM), writes every entry of snd_cs4236_ext_map into the extended registers, writes default values to the input, aux and line-in registers, writes the master volumes with 0xff only for WSS_HW_CS4235 and WSS_HW_CS4239, stores the chip in *rchip and returns 0. On the -ENODEV returns the chip is not freed here and *rchip stays NULL.
note: slice cut the head; real function cs4236_lib.c:252-354. Reviewer right: C1 is only read (line 295) and not programmed; registers C0, C2-C8 are written (305-320).

name: snd_gf1_pokew
prose: Precondition: gus is a GUS card, addr a DRAM address and data a 16-bit value. If gus->interwave is false it logs a debug message but continues. Under gus->reg_lock with interrupts saved and disabled it selects the DRAM I/O low register and writes the low 16 bits of addr, selects the DRAM I/O high register and writes bits 16..23 of addr (addr >> 16 cast to unsigned char), selects the 16-bit DRAM I/O register and writes data, with memory barriers between port writes. Returns nothing.
note: gus_io.c:254-270; previously dropped but this is a real function, so fixed.

name: snd_gf1_peekw
prose: Precondition: gus is a GUS card and addr a DRAM address. If gus->interwave is false it logs a debug message but continues. Under gus->reg_lock with interrupts saved and disabled it writes the low 16 bits of addr to the DRAM I/O low register, bits 16..23 (addr >> 16 as unsigned char) to the DRAM I/O high register, selects the 16-bit DRAM I/O register and returns the 16-bit value read with inw from the data port. There is no error return.
note: gus_io.c:272-288; previously dropped but this is a real function, so fixed.

name: snd_gf1_dram_setmem
prose: Precondition: gus is a GUS card, addr a DRAM address, value a 16-bit pattern, count a byte count. If gus->interwave is false it logs a debug message but continues. It clears bit 0 of addr and halves count (so an odd byte count loses its last byte). Under gus->reg_lock with interrupts saved and disabled it sets the DRAM address (low 16 bits then bits 16..23), selects the 16-bit DRAM I/O register and then writes value with outw to the GF1 data-low port count times (count after halving). Returns nothing and does not check the range.
note: gus_io.c:290-312; previously dropped but this is a real function, so fixed.

name: snd_msndmix_set
prose: Precondition: dev is the msnd device, d a mixer index, left and right percentages. Returns -EINVAL at once if d >= LEVEL_ENTRIES (a negative d is not checked). Otherwise it scales left and right to byte (x * 0xff / 100) and word (x * 0xffff / 100) values and stores the word values in dev->left_levels[d] and dev->right_levels[d] before looking at which control d is. MSND_MIXER_LINE writes the byte values to the line pot position in SMA memory and, if snd_msnd_send_word(...HDEXAR_IN_SET_POTS) returns 0, sends HDEX_AUX_REQ, then returns 0 without the master update. MSND_MIXER_MIC returns -EINVAL for a msndClassic device (levels already stored), otherwise does the same with the mic registers and returns 0. MSND_MIXER_VOLUME writes the word values to the current master volume registers and, like MSND_MIXER_AUX, SYNTH, PCM and IMIX, then runs the master update: update_volm for PCM and IMIX, update_volm for SYNTH only on msndPinnacle, update_potm for AUX, and returns 0. Any other d below LEVEL_ENTRIES returns -EINVAL after its levels were already stored.
note: msnd_pinnacle_mixer.c:181-246. Reviewer right: levels are stored (196-197) before the switch, so the default -EINVAL return (233) and the classic-MIC -EINVAL (210) leave stored levels. update_volm/update_potm macros not expanded.

name: snd_miro_put_double
prose: Precondition: kcontrol is a Miro mixer control whose private_value encodes the ACI get register in bits 0..7 and set register in bits 8..15, ucontrol holds left and right requested values. The set register for the right channel is the encoded one and for the left is that + 8 (or +1 when the right set register is ACI_SET_MASTER); the get register for the left channel is the right one + 1. It first reads both current values with aci_getvalue, logging and returning the negative error right away if either fails (nothing written). For an equalizer control (get register between ACI_GET_EQ1 and ACI_GET_EQ7) it returns -EINVAL if either requested value is outside -0x7f..0x7f; it converts old values above 0x80 to 0x80 - old, and writes each channel with aci_setvalue, as the value itself if non-negative or 0x80 - value if negative. For other controls it returns -EINVAL if either value is outside 0..0x20, converts old values to 0x20 - old, and writes 0x20 - value for each channel. In both cases aci_setvalue is called for left then right and the first negative error is returned immediately (the left write may already have happened). If all writes succeed it returns 1 if left or right differs from its converted old value, else 0.
note: Listed as unnamed excerpt; real function snd_miro_put_double, miro.c:475-582. Reviewer right: the aci_getvalue failure returns (496-507) come before validation and the old prose omitted them.

name: snd_wavefront_midi_output_write
prose: Precondition: card is a wavefront card whose midi state holds two output substreams (internal and external) and the current output_mpu; the caller must not already hold midi->virtual. Returns nothing; max (256) bounds the number of data bytes sent. Phase one is skipped if substream_output[output_mpu] is NULL. Otherwise, while max > 0: it busy-waits up to 30000 polls for output_ready, takes midi->virtual (irqsave) for that iteration, jumps to phase two if mode[output_mpu] lacks MPU401_MODE_OUTPUT; if output is ready it transmits one byte from the output_mpu substream: on success the byte is written with write_data (unless the interface is virtual and the byte is WF_INTERNAL_SWITCH or WF_EXTERNAL_SWITCH) and max is decremented; with nothing to send it decrements istimer (deleting the timer when it reaches 0 or less), clears MPU401_MODE_OUTPUT_TRIGGER for output_mpu and goes to phase two; if the device is not ready it returns from the whole function. Phase two returns if substream_output[!output_mpu] is NULL (this check is made even in non-virtual mode). Then, while max > 0, with the same wait and lock, it picks mpu: in virtual mode the first pass uses the other port (output_mpu ^ 1), in non-virtual mode and on later passes mpu is output_mpu; it returns if mode[mpu] lacks MPU401_MODE_OUTPUT; if that substream has nothing to transmit it does the istimer / trigger-clear step and returns; if the device is ready and mpu differs from output_mpu it writes the internal or external switch byte and sets output_mpu = mpu (without counting max), else transmits one byte as in phase one; if not ready it returns.
note: wavefront_midi.c:112-216. Reviewer right: in non-virtual mode the second loop's mpu is output_mpu (mask forced to 0, lines 183-185), so it does not drain the other port's substream; the other substream is only tested for NULL.

name: wavefront_synth_control
prose: Precondition: acard is the wavefront card and wc a control request with cmd, wbuf, rbuf and status fields. Commands handled before the hardware call, each returning directly: WFC_DISABLE_INTERRUPTS and WFC_ENABLE_INTERRUPTS write the control port and set interrupts_are_midi (wc->status untouched) and return 0; WFC_INTERRUPT_STATUS copies interrupts_are_midi to rbuf[0] and returns 0; WFC_ROMSAMPLES_RDONLY stores wbuf[0] and sets wc->status = 0, returns 0; WFC_IDENTIFY_SLOT_TYPE computes slot = wbuf[0] | wbuf[1] << 7 and, if it is outside 0..WF_MAX_SAMPLE-1, sets wc->status = EINVAL and returns -EINVAL, else sets rbuf[0] to sample_status[slot], status 0, returns 0; WFC_DEBUG_DRIVER stores wbuf[0] in dev->debug and returns 0 (status untouched); WFC_UPLOAD_MULTISAMPLE sets wc->status from wavefront_fetch_multisample and returns 0; WFC_UPLOAD_SAMPLE_ALIAS sets wc->status = EINVAL and returns -EINVAL. WFC_UPLOAD_PATCH first re-encodes the 32-bit patch number in wbuf into two bytes and falls out of the switch. For all other commands, and WFC_UPLOAD_PATCH, it sets wc->status = snd_wavefront_cmd(dev, cmd, rbuf, wbuf). If that status is 0 it post-processes: WFC_REPORT_FREE_MEMORY sets dev->freemem from the decoded 4-byte value in rbuf (rbuf itself is not rewritten), WFC_UPLOAD_PATCH, PROGRAM and EDRUM_PROGRAM demunge rbuf in place, WFC_UPLOAD_SAMPLE_HEADER calls process_sample_hdr, WFC_UPLOAD_SAMPLE_ALIAS logs an error, WFC_VMIDI_OFF and WFC_VMIDI_ON disable or enable the virtual MIDI. On this path the function returns 0 even when snd_wavefront_cmd failed; the failure is only in wc->status.
note: slice cut the head; real function wavefront_synth.c:1515-1640. Reviewer right: demunge_int32 (547-559) only returns a value, so rbuf is not rewritten for WFC_REPORT_FREE_MEMORY.

name: wavefront_do_reset
prose: Precondition: dev is an initialised WaveFront device; ospath names the OS firmware file and is used only when dev->israw is set. Returns 0 on success and 1 on any failure. Steps: wavefront_reset_to_cleanliness (failure goes to the failure path). If dev->israw: wavefront_download_firmware(dev, ospath) (failure goes to the failure path), then dev->israw is cleared, then two WFC_NOOP interrupt waits (osrun_time*HZ and 10*HZ) each followed by a check of dev->irq_ok (failure after either goes to the failure path), then the control port gets 0x80|0x40. Then dev->freemem = wavefront_freemem(dev), failure path if negative; then the MPU-emulation command sequence (write 0xf0, write 1, read), where failure sets dev->debug = 0 and goes to the failure path; then snd_wavefront_cmd(WFC_SET_NVOICES) with 32 voices, failure path on nonzero; then returns 0. The failure path writes 0 to the control port, sets interrupts_are_midi to 0 and returns 1. A failure after the israw clear does not restore israw.
note: slice cut the head; real function wavefront_synth.c:2036-2123 (listed as unnamed init). Old prose was close; rewritten from the code, nothing contradicted. No reviewer claim beyond the name.

name: snd_wss_playback_format
prose: Precondition: chip is a WSS chip, params the hardware params, pdfr the playback format register value. Returns nothing. Holds chip->mce_mutex for the whole function. For WSS_HW_CS4231A or any CS4232-mask hardware, under reg_lock: if the rate nibble (low 4 bits) of image[CS4231_PLAYBK_FORMAT] equals that of pdfr, it sets bit 0x10 of ALT_FEATURE_1, stores pdfr in image[PLAYBK_FORMAT] and writes it, clears bit 0x10 again, waits 100 us and sets full_calib = 0; with a different rate nibble it does nothing in this branch. For WSS_HW_AD1845 it writes pdfr & 0xf0 to the format register and then the upper and lower bytes of the sample rate (params_rate) to the AD1845 frequency registers, setting full_calib = 0. If full_calib is still 1 (other hardware, or the CS4231A/CS4232 case with a different rate) it calls snd_wss_mce_up, then under reg_lock: if the hardware is not WSS_HW_INTERWAVE and single_dma is not set, then if IFACE_CTRL has CS4231_RECORD_ENABLE the rate nibble of pdfr is replaced by that of the record format image and in either case image[PLAYBK_FORMAT] is left unchanged; otherwise (InterWave or single_dma) image[PLAYBK_FORMAT] = pdfr; the (possibly adjusted) pdfr is written to the playback format register. It then waits 100 us for WSS_HW_OPL3SA2 and calls snd_wss_mce_down.
note: wss_lib.c:606-661. Reviewer right: in the non-InterWave, non-single_dma case image[CS4231_PLAYBK_FORMAT] is not updated (lines 648-651), only the register write uses pdfr.

name: n64audio_init
prose: Module init function with no arguments; its only statement returns platform_driver_probe(&n64audio_driver, n64audio_probe), so it returns whatever that call returns: 0 on success or the negative error that platform_driver_probe reports (including a probe function's own errno). The function itself adds no -ENODEV or other value.
note: snd-n64.c:364-367. Reviewer right (prose claimed -ENODEV specifically); internals of platform_driver_probe not read.

name: AtaSetBass
prose: Precondition: bass is a VOXWARE tone value. It sets dmasound.bass to the dB value TONE_VOXWARE_TO_DB(bass) (-12 for bass below 0, 12 for bass above 100, otherwise (bass - 50) * 6 / 25), sends that value to the LM1992 chip with atari_microwire_cmd(MW_LM1992_BASS(dmasound.bass)), and returns TONE_DB_TO_VOXWARE(dmasound.bass), i.e. (db * 25 + 5 or -5) / 6 + 50 (the +5 for positive db, -5 otherwise). There is no error return; it changes the global dmasound.bass and writes to the hardware.
note: dmasound_atari.c:878-883. Reviewer right (old contract omitted the global update and the microwire command); contract left empty.

name: AtaSetTreble
prose: Precondition: treble is a VOXWARE tone value. It sets dmasound.treble to the dB value TONE_VOXWARE_TO_DB(treble) (-12 for treble below 0, 12 for treble above 100, otherwise (treble - 50) * 6 / 25), sends that value to the LM1992 chip with atari_microwire_cmd(MW_LM1992_TREBLE(dmasound.treble)), and returns TONE_DB_TO_VOXWARE(dmasound.treble), i.e. (db * 25 + 5 or -5) / 6 + 50 (the +5 for positive db, -5 otherwise). There is no error return; it changes the global dmasound.treble and writes to the hardware.
note: dmasound_atari.c:886-891. Reviewer right (old contract omitted the global update and the microwire command); contract left empty.

name: AmiMixerIoctl
prose: Precondition: cmd is an OSS mixer ioctl command and arg a user pointer to an int. Each handled command returns the result of IOCTL_OUT, which is the value itself if it is negative and otherwise the result of put_user to arg (0, or -EFAULT on a bad pointer); an unhandled cmd returns -EINVAL. SOUND_MIXER_READ_DEVMASK outputs SOUND_MASK_VOLUME | SOUND_MASK_TREBLE; READ_RECMASK outputs 0; READ_STEREODEVS outputs SOUND_MASK_VOLUME; READ_VOLUME outputs the left volume (volume_left * 100 / 64) | the right volume (volume_right * 100 / 64) << 8; READ_TREBLE outputs dmasound.treble. For SOUND_MIXER_WRITE_VOLUME and SOUND_MIXER_WRITE_TREBLE it first reads an int from arg with get_user (IOCTL_IN returns the get_user error, -EFAULT, from this function if that fails), calls dmasound_set_volume(data) or dmasound_set_treble(data) and outputs its return value through IOCTL_OUT.
note: dmasound_paula.c:619-643 with IOCTL_IN/IOCTL_OUT (dmasound.h:46-55) read. Reviewer mechanical (prose lists EFAULT/EINVAL, contract omits): right; contract left empty.

name: snd_ac97_mixer
prose: Precondition: bus, template and rac97 are non-NULL (snd_BUG_ON, returns -EINVAL otherwise) and template->num is below 4 (else -EINVAL); *rac97 is set to NULL before further checks. Returns -EBUSY if bus->codec[template->num] is already taken, -ENOMEM if the kzalloc of the codec fails. It copies template fields into the new snd_ac97, registers it in bus->codec[num], initialises its mutexes (and the power work under CONFIG_SND_AC97_POWER_SAVE) and, with a PCI device, reads the subsystem ids. If bus->ops->reset exists it is called and the reset wait is skipped; otherwise it reads the vendor id and, unless the id is nonzero, not -1 and the codec is flagged AC97_DEFAULT_POWER_OFF, it resets the audio and/or modem part and waits (failure to respond is only a warning). It then reads the id again; if the id is 0 or 0xffffffff and AC97_SCAP_DETECT_BY_VENDOR is not set it logs, frees the codec with snd_ac97_free and returns -EIO. It probes audio capability (record-gain write test) and modem capability; if the codec is neither audio nor modem it frees it and returns -EACCES. Without bus->ops->reset it waits up to 5 s (audio) or 100 ms (modem) for ready bits (timeouts are warnings only), sets addr, programs extended-status bits and determines sample rates and SPDIF/surround/LFE capability from ext_id, calls bus->ops->init if present, builds the codec name, appends it to the card mixer name when it fits, adds the component string with snd_component_add, builds the audio mixer (snd_ac97_mixer_build) and/or the modem controls (snd_ac97_modem_build); snd_component_add failure frees the codec and returns its error and a mixer or modem build failure frees the codec and returns -ENOMEM. For audio codecs it calls update_power_regs, then snd_ac97_proc_init and registers the codec with snd_device_new(card, SNDRV_DEV_CODEC, ...); on failure it frees the codec and returns the error, on success it stores the codec in *rac97 and returns 0, after which the sound card device (snd_ac97_dev_free) owns and frees the codec.
note: slice cut the head; real function ac97_codec.c:2048-2346. Reviewer right: after snd_device_new succeeds the card owns the codec through ops.dev_free = snd_ac97_dev_free (line 2058); the caller does not free it. Many callee helpers not read in detail.

name: patch_sigmatel_stac9700
prose: Precondition: ac97 is a codec instance. It only sets ac97->build_ops to &patch_sigmatel_stac9700_ops and returns 0; it performs no register reads or writes and has no other return.
note: slice cut the head; real function ac97_patch.c:967-971 (a four-line function). Reviewer WRONG: the reviewer's claim of register reads/writes and a MULTICHN write does not match this function; any such register access would be in the build_ops callbacks, not here.

name: snd_ac97_stac9758_phonesel_put
prose: Precondition: kcontrol is the STAC9758 phone-select control and ucontrol holds the enumerated item. It returns ac97_update_bits_page(ac97, AC97_SIGMATEL_IOMISC, 3, item[0], 0). That helper, holding ac97->page_mutex, reads and saves the page bits of AC97_INT_PAGING, selects page 0, calls snd_ac97_update_bits on the register with mask 3 and value item[0] (only the low 2 bits are applied) and restores the saved page, returning the result of the register update: 1 if the cached register value changed (the new value is written to the codec), 0 if unchanged, or -EINVAL if snd_ac97_valid_reg rejects the register. The paging register updates' results are ignored.
note: ac97_patch.c:1163-1169, ac97_update_bits_page (52-63), snd_ac97_update_bits (380-406). Reviewer MIXED: right that the normal result is the change flag 0/1, but a negative -EINVAL from snd_ac97_valid_reg is possible through snd_ac97_update_bits.

name: vortex_game_open
prose: Precondition: gameport carries a vortex_t as port data, mode is GAMEPORT_MODE_COOKED or GAMEPORT_MODE_RAW. For GAMEPORT_MODE_COOKED it reads VORTEX_CTRL2 and writes it back with CTRL2_GAME_ADCMODE set, then calls msleep(VORTEX_GAME_DWAIT) itself, then returns 0. For GAMEPORT_MODE_RAW it reads VORTEX_CTRL2 and writes it back with CTRL2_GAME_ADCMODE cleared and returns 0 without sleeping. Any other mode returns -1 and touches no register.
note: au88x0_game.c:59-80. Reviewer right: the function itself sleeps in cooked mode (line 68) and the CTRL2 writes are side effects the old contract omitted; contract left empty.

name: snd_cs46xx_playback_trigger
prose: Precondition: substream is a cs46xx playback substream; cmd is a PCM trigger command. When CONFIG_SND_CS46XX_NEW_DSP is defined, it first returns -ENXIO if the stream's cpcm->pcm_channel is NULL (without that option no such check exists). SNDRV_PCM_TRIGGER_START and RESUME: with the new DSP it writes 0x80008000 to the reader SCB volume control (unmute), links the PCM channel with cs46xx_dsp_pcm_link if it is unlinked, and calls snd_cs46xx_playback_transfer if runtime->periods != CS46XX_FRAGS; without it, under chip->reg_lock it calls snd_cs46xx_playback_transfer on the same condition, then ORs chip->play_ctl into the low 16 bits of the BA1_PCTL register value kept from the peek (tmp & 0xffff). SNDRV_PCM_TRIGGER_STOP and SUSPEND: with the new DSP it writes 0xffffffff to the SCB volume control (mute) and unlinks the channel if it is linked; without it, under reg_lock it writes BA1_PCTL with the upper 16 bits cleared (tmp & 0x0000ffff). Any other cmd returns -EINVAL; otherwise it returns 0.
note: cs46xx_lib.c:941-1002. Reviewer right: the NULL pcm_channel case returns -ENXIO (lines 950-952), but only under CONFIG_SND_CS46XX_NEW_DSP.

name: select_rom
prose: Pure function mapping a pitch value to a ROM selector; it reads no state. In order of tests it returns 1 if pitch is strictly between 0x00428f5c and 0x01b851ec, 2 if pitch equals 0x01d66666 or 0x01d66667, 3 if pitch equals 0x02000000, 0 if pitch is at most 0x08000000 (this covers all remaining values up to that bound, including values at or below 0x00428f5c and between the other ranges), and -ENOENT if pitch is greater than 0x08000000.
note: ctatc.c:223-240. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits ENOENT): right; contract left empty. The comment says 0.26 <= pitch <= 1.72 but the code bounds are strict.

name: _snd_emu10k1_init_efx
prose: Precondition: emu is an SB Live (non-Audigy) emu10k1 whose fx8010.extin_mask and extout_mask say which external inputs and outputs exist. Returns 0 on success, -ENOMEM if any of the four allocations fails, -EIO if its own accounting overflows, or the error of the final steps. It allocates the icode structure, a 256+160+160+2*512 entry u32 map (gpr_map, tram data and address maps, code), a SND_EMU10K1_GPR_CONTROLS-sized control array and a pcm record; on a failed allocation it frees the ones already made and returns -ENOMEM. It marks all GPRs and TRAM lines valid, names the code, and assembles the DSP program: the FX bus inputs, an S/PDIF raw-PCM playback pointer routine (the instruction run in the slice at lines 1888-1936, built around the trigger and running GPRs), per-source playback and capture volume and switch stages (wave, synth, surround, center, LFE, front), per-input stages for each external input whose bit is set in extin_mask (AC97, S/PDIF TTL, zoom video, optical, line1, coax, line2), two tone-control entries (bass and treble) plus a tone switch, and output stages for each external output set in extout_mask, filling the controls array as it goes. After this it returns -EIO (via the common cleanup) if the GPR counter gpr passed the temporary area start tmp or if the control count exceeds SND_EMU10K1_GPR_CONTROLS (snd_BUG), pads the rest of instruction memory, calls snd_emu10k1_fx8010_tram_setup and returns its negative error, otherwise sets the control table in icode, sets emu->support_tlv = 1 while calling snd_emu10k1_icode_poke, clears it again, and if that succeeded calls snd_emu10k1_ipcm_poke; the err of those calls is returned. All paths after the allocations free ipcm, controls, gpr_map and icode before returning.
note: Listed as snd_emu10k1_init_fx8010 and dropped; that name does not exist and the slice (emufx.c:1888-2139) is the middle of _snd_emu10k1_init_efx (1793-2344), so fixed under the real name. Large function: the OP() instruction lists and the details of the individual volume/switch stages were skimmed (non-OP lines read in full), not checked instruction by instruction.

name: snd_emu10k1_gpr_ctl_put
prose: Precondition: kcontrol->private_value points to a valid snd_emu10k1_fx8010_ctl whose vcount values, min, max, translation and gpr[] indices are consistent; ucontrol holds at least vcount integer values. For each i below ctl->vcount it clamps the new value to [ctl->min, ctl->max], sets change = 1 if it differs from the stored ctl->value[i], stores it in ctl->value[i] and writes the translated value to the GPR emu->gpr_base + ctl->gpr[i]: unchanged for TRANSLATION_NONE, ~val for NEGATE, db_table[val] for TABLE100, 0x80000000 if val is 100 else -(int)db_table[val] for NEG_TABLE100, onoff_table[val] for ONOFF. For TRANSLATION_BASS and TRANSLATION_TREBLE it requires ctl->count to be a multiple of 5 with count / 5 equal to vcount, otherwise it sets the result to -EIO and stops; if the check passes it writes the five table entries bass_table[val][j] or treble_table[val][j] to ctl->gpr[j * vcount + i] for j = 0..4, so these two translations access 5 * vcount gpr entries. It returns 1 if any value changed, 0 if none, or -EIO (values handled before the failing step stay written and stored). There is no locking in this function.
note: emufx.c:360-415. Reviewer right: BASS/TREBLE use ctl->gpr[j * vcount + i] (5 * vcount entries), guarded by the count check (393, 401).

name: snd_emu10k1_mixer
prose: Precondition: emu is an emu10k1 card, pcm_device and multi_device are the PCM device numbers to attach controls to. Returns 0 on success or a negative error; controls added before an error stay added. If card_capabilities->ac97_chip is set: it creates the AC97 bus (error returned) and the AC97 mixer; if the mixer fails it returns that error when ac97_chip == 1, otherwise logs that AC97 is optional, frees the bus and continues at the no_ac97 branch (naming the mixer); on success it adjusts AC97 registers for Audigy (master 0 dB, capture source mic, mono output) or for non-Audigy cards (STAC9758 rear handling, surround and center/LFE masters) and removes the listed unused controls (remove_ctl) for the card type. Else, with i2c_adc set it removes the i2c-ADC list; otherwise it sets the card mixer name to "EMU APS", "SB Audigy" or "Emu10k1". It then renames controls from the table matching the card (Audigy variants or emu10k1), removes some center/LFE controls for subsystem 0x80401102, and renames four controls for subsystem 0x20071102. It then creates and adds the send routing, send volume and attenuation controls (device = pcm_device) and the three EFX equivalents (device = multi_device); each snd_ctl_new1 result is checked and gives -ENOMEM if NULL, and a snd_ctl_add error is returned. It adds the S/PDIF mask and S/PDIF controls for non-ecard, non-emu_model cards, the shared S/PDIF control for Audigy (not emu_model) or non-ecard emu10k1, the P16V mixer for ca0151 chips, and for emu_model (EMU1010) cards it sets default routing sources, applies them under the FPGA lock, adds the clock source and clock fallback controls, ADC/DAC pad controls, optical controls (unless no_adat) and the source mixers. For this clock source and clock fallback, the snd_ctl_new1 results are not checked, so a NULL result is passed to snd_ctl_add which then returns -EINVAL, not -ENOMEM. For i2c_adc cards it adds the capture source and the i2c volume controls, and for ac97_chip plus Audigy it adds the capture boost control. It returns 0 at the end.
note: slice cut the head; real function emumixer.c:1987-2376. Reviewer right: the EMU1010 clock source / fallback controls are created without a NULL check (2322-2327) and snd_ctl_add(NULL) returns -EINVAL (control.c:515-516).

name: intel8x0_measure_ac97_clock
prose: Precondition: chip is an initialised intel8x0 with ac97 and pcm[0] set up. Returns nothing. It returns at once, doing nothing, if chip->ac97_bus->clock is not 48000 (set by a module option) or if chip->inside_vm is set and the ac97_clock parameter is 0. At the __again label: if pcm[0] playback substream is missing or its dma_buffer.bytes is below INTEL8X0_TESTBUF_SIZE it warns and returns; otherwise it points the ICHD_PCMOUT channel at that DMA buffer (physbuf, size and fragsize set, substream cleared to NULL), and if snd_ac97_set_rate(ac97[0], AC97_PCM_FRONT_DAC_RATE, 48000) fails it logs and returns (the channel fields just written stay changed). Otherwise it sets up periods and, under reg_lock, sets in_measurement = 1, starts the DMA engine (ALI chips through the ALI_DMACR register) and records the start time; it sleeps 50 ms; then, under reg_lock, reads the current position (retrying up to about 1000 times while the position reads as 0 or changes), computes pos, clears in_measurement, takes the stop time, stops and resets the DMA channel (with unbounded polling loops waiting for the hardware). If pos is 0 (unreliable) or the elapsed time is 0, or the computed clock is below 40000 or at least 60000, it retries from __again after msleep(300) if fewer than 3 attempts were made; otherwise it ends. If the measured clock is in (40500,41500) it sets ac97_bus->clock to 41000; if in (43600,44600) to 44100; if outside [47500,48500] it sets clock = clock * 48000 / measured; else it leaves the clock unchanged. At the end label (reached after a successful measurement or after the third failed attempt) it logs the clock and calls snd_ac97_update_power(ac97[0], AC97_PCM_FRONT_DAC_RATE, 0). The two early returns after the checks (no buffer, set_rate failure) skip that final log and power call.
note: Listed name snd_intel8x0_measure_ac97_clock does not exist; the function is intel8x0_measure_ac97_clock, intel8x0.c:2627-2747 (slice cut the head). Old prose largely agreed with the code; rewritten from it.

name: lola_sample_rate_convert
prose: Pure function decoding a coded sample-rate field into Hz, reading no state. Returns 0 for an invalid code. Base rate from (coded & 0x3): 0 gives 48000, 1 gives 44100, 2 gives 32000, 3 returns 0. Multiplier from (coded & 0x1c): 0 and (4 << 2) leave it unchanged, (1 << 2) doubles it, (2 << 2) multiplies by 4, (5 << 2) halves it, (6 << 2) divides it by 4 (integer division), and any other value ((3 << 2) or (7 << 2)) returns 0. Adjustment from (coded & 0x60): 0 leaves it, (1 << 5) gives freq * 999 / 1000, (2 << 5) gives freq * 1001 / 1000, and (3 << 5) returns 0. Bits above bit 6 are ignored. The result is the unsigned frequency after these three steps.
note: lola_clock.c:15-46. Reviewer right that the old contract omitted the no-side-effects guarantee; contract left empty.

name: snd_mixart_add_ref_pipe
prose: Precondition: chip is a mixart card; pcm_number selects analog (MIXART_PCM_ANALOG) or digital; capture selects capture or playback; monitoring is nonzero for a monitoring reference. Returns a pointer to the matching pipe (pipe_in_ana, pipe_in_dig, pipe_out_ana or pipe_out_dig inside chip) or NULL. It returns NULL if monitoring is 0 and the pipe's references count is already at least the stream count (MIXART_CAPTURE_STREAMS or MIXART_PLAYBACK_STREAMS). If the pipe status is PIPE_UNDEFINED it allocates a request/response buffer (NULL return if kmalloc fails), fills a streaming-group request (stream_count, two channels, latency 256, left connector, and for each stream the maximum sizes, a flow entry index j, the flowinfo and bufferinfo entries and the buffer id), and sends it with snd_mixart_send_msg; if that returns an error or the response status is nonzero it logs, frees the buffer and returns NULL. On success it stores the response's group id in pipe->group_uid and the response's stream_count in pipe->stream_count, sets pipe->status to PIPE_STOPPED (a constant, not taken from the response) and frees the buffer. In all non-NULL cases it then sets pipe->monitoring = 1 if monitoring is nonzero, otherwise increments pipe->references, and returns the pipe.
note: slice cut the head; real function mixart.c:215-325. Reviewer right: pipe->status = PIPE_STOPPED (line 317), not a firmware status.

name: snd_mixart_send_msg
prose: Precondition: mgr is the mixart manager, request the message, max_resp_size the capacity of resp_data. It sends the request under mgr->msg_lock with send_msg (marked as answer pending); a nonzero error from send_msg is returned at once. Otherwise it queues itself on mgr->msg_sleep as an uninterruptible waiter and sleeps up to MSG_TIMEOUT_JIFFIES; if the timeout expires with no wake-up it logs and returns -EIO. Otherwise it fetches the answer with get_msg under the lock into resp_data (capacity max_resp_size) and returns get_msg's result: 0, or -EINVAL when the response size from the card is below MSG_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE or larger than max_resp_size (in which case the data is not copied) or when the outbound free head pointer is out of range. If the response message_id differs from the request's it only logs "RESPONSE ERROR!" and that does not change the returned value.
note: mixart_core.c:219-263; get_msg's returns read at 70-120. Reviewer right: get_msg's -EINVAL paths (79-84, 103-105) were omitted by the old prose.

name: pcxhr_get_clock_reg
prose: Precondition: mgr is the pcxhr manager (mgr->use_clock_type selects the clock source), rate is a sample rate; reg and freq are output pointers. On success it writes the clock register selector to *reg and the actual frequency to *freq and returns 0. For PCXHR_CLOCK_TYPE_INTERNAL it maps rates 48000, 24000, 12000, 32000, 16000, 8000, 44100, 22050, 11025, 192000, 96000, 176400, 88200, 128000 and 64000 to quartz selectors with freq = rate; any other rate selects PCXHR_FREQ_PLL, computes the PLL register and real frequency with pcxhr_pll_freq_register (its nonzero error is returned) and writes the PLL register to the card with CMD_ACCESS_IO_WRITE through pcxhr_send_msg (a negative result is logged and returned); in that PLL case *freq is the PLL's real frequency. Word clock, AES sync and AES 1 to 4 clock types select fixed selectors with freq = rate. Any other use_clock_type returns -EINVAL. *reg and *freq are not written on any error return.
note: Listed as pcxhr_get_clock_type (dropped); that name is not in the file and the slice (pcxhr.c:1-301) contains pcxhr_get_clock_reg (234-304), so fixed under the real name. pcxhr_pll_freq_register read only at its end (lines 195-205).

name: setsamplerate
prose: Precondition: cif is the command interface, intdec points to two selector bytes (a value of 0xff means skip that slot), rate is the target rate. It computes D = 48000, M = (rate, or 47999 when rate is 48000) * 65536 and then N = M % D and M = M / D. It loops i over 0 and 1: for a selector that is not 0xff it repeatedly sends the SSRC command with (D, M, N) and reads it back with the RSRC command; the retry loop repeats while the returned words 1, 2 and 3 all differ from D, M and N respectively (the && of the three differences) and i++ < MAX_WRITE_RETRY. The retry counter is the same variable as the outer slot index, so retries advance i and can end the outer loop early. If i is greater than MAX_WRITE_RETRY after the loop it logs and returns -EIO. Otherwise intdec advances and it returns 0, which can happen without the second selector having been processed. Results of SEND_SSRC and SEND_RSRC themselves are not checked here.
note: slice cut the head; real function riptide.c:1023-1054. Reviewer right: the retry condition increments i (line 1044), so the second selector can be skipped and the function still returns 0. SEND_SSRC/SEND_RSRC macros not read.

name: #define rme9652_decode_latency(x)  (((x)>>1)&0x7)
prose: Function-like macro, not a C function: rme9652_decode_latency(x) expands to ((x) >> 1) & 0x7, the latency field (bits 1..3) of a control-register value, an integer 0..7. It evaluates x once and has no side effects or state of its own.
note: rme9652.c:157. Previously dropped as a non-function; the macro does real bit arithmetic rather than forwarding, so kept as a fix with the macro definition head as name.

name: #define rme9652_decode_spdif_in(x) (((x)>>14)&0x3)
prose: Function-like macro, not a C function: rme9652_decode_spdif_in(x) expands to ((x) >> 14) & 0x3, the S/PDIF input selection field (bits 14..15) of a control-register value, an integer 0..3. It evaluates x once and has no side effects or state of its own.
note: rme9652.c:161. Previously dropped as a non-function; same reasoning as rme9652_decode_latency.

name: #define RME9652_REV15_buf_pos(x) ((((x)&0xE0000000)>>26)|((x)&RME9652_buf_pos))
prose: Function-like macro, not a C function: RME9652_REV15_buf_pos(x) expands to (((x) & 0xE0000000) >> 26) | ((x) & RME9652_buf_pos), that is the register's bits 31..29 moved down to bits 5..3 ORed with the masked bits (RME9652_buf_pos is 0x000FFC0) of x. It evaluates its argument twice, so an argument with side effects would be evaluated twice; it has no state of its own.
note: rme9652.c:104. Previously dropped as a non-function; macro with real arithmetic, kept as a fix.

name: pdacf_interrupt
prose: Hard-IRQ handler: irq is unused, dev is the snd_pdacf chip. Returns IRQ_HANDLED immediately, without reading the hardware, unless chip->chip_status has PDAUDIOCF_STAT_IS_CONFIGURED set and both IS_STALE and IS_SUSPENDED clear. Otherwise it reads the ISR register; if the IRQLVL or IRQOVR bit is set it logs an overrun for IRQOVR and sets wake_thread when chip->pcm_substream exists (the following 'stat |= PDAUDIOCF_IRQAKM' only changes the local variable, which is not used again). Then, if get_irq_regs() is non-NULL (called from a real interrupt, not a forced thread), it calls snd_ak4117_check_rate_and_errors(chip->ak4117, 0). It returns IRQ_WAKE_THREAD if wake_thread was set, otherwise IRQ_HANDLED. It does not itself transfer PCM data.
note: slice cut the head; real function pdaudiocf_irq.c:16-39. Reviewer WRONG: the code does the SUSPENDED/STALE/CONFIGURED check (22-25), the ak4117 call (36-37) and returns IRQ_WAKE_THREAD (38); the PCM transfer is not in this function.

name: snd_pdacf_pcm_new
prose: Precondition: chip is a snd_pdacf with an initialised card and ak4117. It calls snd_pcm_new(chip->card, "PDAudioCF", 0, 0, 1, &pcm) (no playback, one capture stream) and returns that negative error if it fails. Otherwise it installs pdacf_pcm_capture_ops for capture, sets up vmalloc-managed buffers, sets pcm->private_data = chip, pcm->info_flags = 0, pcm->nonatomic = true, copies the card short name into pcm->name and stores the pcm in chip->pcm. Then it calls snd_ak4117_build on the capture substream and returns its negative error if it fails (the pcm and chip->pcm stay set; nothing is freed here), else returns 0.
note: Listed as pdacf_pcm_create (dropped); the slice (pdaudiocf_pcm.c:254-273) is the body of snd_pdacf_pcm_new (249-273), a real function, so fixed under its real name.

name: snd_pmac_daca_init
prose: Precondition: chip is a snd_pmac. It calls request_module("i2c-powermac"), then kzalloc's a pmac_daca (returns -ENOMEM if that fails) and stores it in chip->mixer_data with chip->mixer_free = daca_cleanup and amp_on = 1. It sets the I2C address, init_client and name, and calls snd_pmac_keywest_init, returning a negative error without freeing mix here (the allocation is left for the mixer_free callback). It then sets the card mixer name to "PowerMac DACA" and adds each control from daca_mixers with snd_ctl_add(snd_ctl_new1(...)), returning the first negative error (the snd_ctl_new1 result is not checked here). With CONFIG_PM it sets chip->resume = daca_resume, and it returns 0.
note: Listed as daca_init; the real exported function is snd_pmac_daca_init, daca.c:240-277 (slice shows the tail), so fixed under the real name.

name: mchp_pdmc_trigger
prose: Precondition: substream and dai belong to a mchp_pdmc device; cmd is a trigger command. SNDRV_PCM_TRIGGER_START, RESUME and PAUSE_RELEASE set the PDMCEN bits (dd->pdmcen) in MCHP_PDMC_MR, run mchp_pdmc_noise_filter_workaround, write MCHP_PDMC_IER with dd->suspend_irq | RXOVR | RXUDR and then clear dd->suspend_irq. SNDRV_PCM_TRIGGER_SUSPEND first saves MCHP_PDMC_IMR into dd->suspend_irq and falls through. SUSPEND and STOP both write MCHP_PDMC_IDR with dd->suspend_irq | RXOVR | RXUDR (disabling those interrupts; for STOP, dd->suspend_irq holds whatever value it had before, it is not read) and fall through. PAUSE_PUSH, and the fall-through from SUSPEND and STOP, clear the PDMCEN bits in MCHP_PDMC_MR. Any other cmd returns -EINVAL. In all other cases it returns 0 (with DEBUG defined it also logs MR, CFGR and IMR first).
note: mchp-pdmc.c:640-690. Reviewer right: STOP (and SUSPEND) also write IDR to disable interrupts (669-670); PAUSE_PUSH is the case that only disables the channels.

name: acp_i2s_hwparams
prose: Precondition: substream, params and dai describe an AMD ACP I2S stream; the chip info comes from dev_get_drvdata(dai->component->dev->parent). Returns 0 or -EINVAL. It first maps the sample format to a transfer resolution (U8 and S8 give 0, S16_LE 2, S24_LE 4, S32_LE 5; any other format returns -EINVAL before touching hardware). It picks the ITER (playback) or IRER (capture) register and the format register for dai->driver->id equal to I2S_BT_INSTANCE, I2S_SP_INSTANCE or I2S_HS_INSTANCE (any other id logs and returns -EINVAL) and stores the resolution in chip->xfer_tx_resolution or xfer_rx_resolution at index id - 1. It then writes the resolution (shifted left by 3) into the sample-length field of that register. If chip->tdm_mode it sets bit 1 of the same register and writes the saved TDM format (tx or rx) of that dai to the format register. If rsrc->soc_mclk is set it computes bclk_div_val and lrclk_div_val: for S16_LE from the rate (8000, 16000, 24000, 32000, 44100/48000, 88200/96000, 192000 give 768, 384, 256, 192, 128, 64, 32 with lrclk 32), for S32_LE half of those with lrclk 64; other rates or any other format return -EINVAL (the register writes above already happened); then, for rates 8000, 16000, 24000, 48000, 96000 and 192000, 2 channels leave the dividers, 4, 8, 16 or 32 channels shift bclk down and lrclk up by 1, 2, 3 or 4 bits, and any other channel count only logs an error and keeps the unscaled values; other rates get no channel scaling. It stores the results in chip->lrclk_div and chip->bclk_div and returns 0.
note: Listed as acp_i2s_hw_params and dropped; that name is not in the file and the slice (acp-i2s.c:266-517) spans acp_i2s_hwparams (193-385) and acp_i2s_trigger, so fixed as acp_i2s_hwparams. Old prose agreed on -EINVAL; rewritten from the code. acp_i2s_trigger was not part of this listing.

name: arizona_hpdet_irq
prose: Precondition: data is the arizona_priv for the jack; runs as the HPDET interrupt handler. It takes info->lock for the whole body. If info->hpdet_active is false it logs a warning, unlocks and returns IRQ_NONE. Otherwise it reads the jack's mechanical state; if the cable is removed (state 0) it skips to the done label. Else it calls arizona_hpdet_read: -EAGAIN jumps to the out label (unlock, return IRQ_HANDLED, hpdet_active left as is), another negative value jumps to done, otherwise it is the reading. It resets the impedance range and poll bits, calls arizona_hpdet_do_id(info, &reading, &mic): -EAGAIN jumps to out, another negative value to done, and with 0 it reports SND_JACK_LINEOUT when the reading is 5000 or more and SND_JACK_HEADPHONE otherwise through snd_soc_jack_report. The done label resets the range and poll bits again, removes the headphone clamp, clears the ID GPIO (CONFIG_GPIOLIB_LEGACY and id_gpio nonzero), restarts mic detection when the cable is present and a mic was found (arizona_start_mic when state and (mic or info->mic)), and if info->hpdet_active is still set does pm_runtime_put_autosuspend and clears hpdet_active; it sets info->hpdet_done = true when state is nonzero. All paths other than the spurious one unlock and return IRQ_HANDLED. When arizona_hpdet_do_id returns -EAGAIN for a retry it calls arizona_start_hpdet_acc_id, which can itself fail, report headphone and clear hpdet_active; in that case no retry is pending although this handler took the out path.
note: slice cut the head; real function arizona-jack.c:534-618 with arizona_hpdet_do_id (460-532) and arizona_start_hpdet_acc_id (671-717) read. Reviewer right: the do_id retry path (507-513) can leave hpdet_active false if arizona_start_hpdet_acc_id fails (716).

name: aw88399_dev_fw_update
prose: Precondition: aw88399 is the codec instance, up_dsp_fw_en says whether to reload the DSP firmware, force_up_en forces an update. Returns 0 or a negative error. It returns 0 without doing anything if prof_cur equals prof_index and force_up_en is AW88399_FORCE_UPDATE_OFF. It returns -EPERM if fw_status is AW88399_DEV_FW_FAILED. It looks up the profile name and data for prof_index and returns the helper's error if either lookup fails. It writes the register section with aw_dev_reg_update (error logged and returned). Then it mutes the amplifier (aw88399_dev_mute(true)), disables the DSP if dsp_cfg is AW88399_DEV_DSP_WORK, selects the OSC memory clock and checks the SRAM with aw_dev_check_sram, which itself takes and releases aw_dev->dsp_lock around its DSP accesses and returns -EPERM on a mismatch (this function takes no lock directly). If up_dsp_fw_en it updates the DSP firmware section; then it updates the DSP config section. A failure of the SRAM check, firmware update or config update goes to the error label, which selects the PLL memory clock again and returns the error (the amplifier stays muted and the DSP stays disabled on those paths, and prof_cur is not updated). On success it selects the PLL memory clock, sets prof_cur = prof_index and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function aw88399.c:1214-1292. Reviewer right: aw_dev_check_sram does mutex_lock/unlock of dsp_lock (aw88399.c:1018, 1035, 1039), so the function acquires and releases that lock through the callee.
